```{r}
source("R/inspection_analysis.R")

source("R/interactive_visualizations.R")
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "—")
if (!knitr::is_latex_output() && !interactive_output()) {
  knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = "2026_hall_of_shame_markdown_files/figure-commonmark/")
}

escape_latex_str <- function(x) {
  replacements <- c(
    "\\" = "\\textbackslash{}", "&" = "\\&", "%" = "\\%", "$" = "\\$",
    "#" = "\\#", "_" = "\\_", "{" = "\\{", "}" = "\\}",
    "~" = "\\textasciitilde{}", "^" = "\\textasciicircum{}"
  )
  vapply(strsplit(x, "", fixed = TRUE), function(chars) {
    paste0(ifelse(chars %in% names(replacements), replacements[chars], chars), collapse = "")
  }, character(1))
}

report_table <- function(data, caption, digits = 0) {
  latex <- knitr::is_latex_output()
  if (latex) {
    data <- mutate(data, across(where(is.character), escape_latex_str))
    data$name <- paste0("\\href{", data$REPORT, "}{", data$name, "}")
  } else {
    data$name <- paste0("[", gsub("|", "&#124;", data$name, fixed = TRUE), "](", data$REPORT, ")")
  }
  data <- select(data, -REPORT)
  names(data)[names(data) == "name"] <- "Facility"
  alignment <- ifelse(vapply(data, is.numeric, logical(1)), "r", "l")
  table <- kable(
    data, caption = caption, digits = digits, escape = FALSE, align = alignment,
    format = if (latex) "latex" else "pipe", booktabs = TRUE, longtable = TRUE
  )
  if (latex) {
    widths <- alignment
    widths[names(data) == "Facility"] <- "p{4.2cm}"
    widths[names(data) == "Purpose"] <- "p{2.2cm}"
    table <- sub(
      paste0("{", paste0(alignment, collapse = ""), "}"),
      paste0("{", paste0(widths, collapse = ""), "}"), table, fixed = TRUE
    )
  }
  knitr::asis_output(paste(table, collapse = "\n"))
}

all_inspections <- read.csv(
  "out/violations_by_inspection.csv", colClasses = c(encounter = "character", id = "character")
) |>
  mutate(inspect_dt = as.Date(inspect_dt))
inspections <- all_inspections |>
  filter(inspect_dt >= as.Date("2026-01-01"), inspect_dt < as.Date("2027-01-01")) |>
  rank_inspections()
yearly <- read.csv("out/violations_by_year.csv", colClasses = c(id = "character")) |>
  filter(inspect_yr == 2026)
initial_yearly <- yearly |>
  filter(NUM_INITIAL_INSPECTIONS > 0) |>
  mutate(SEVERITY_RANK = min_rank(data.frame(
    high = -AVG_INITIAL_HIGH, medium = -AVG_INITIAL_MEDIUM, low = -AVG_INITIAL_LOW
  ))) |>
  arrange(SEVERITY_RANK, id)
stopifnot(nrow(inspections) > 0, nrow(initial_yearly) > 0)
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
period_start <- min(inspections$inspect_dt)
period_end <- max(inspections$inspect_dt)
category_audit <- read.csv("out/category_severity_audit.csv") |>
  filter(inspect_yr == 2026)
followup_pairs <- match_followups(inspections)
severity_top <- head(inspections$encounter, 20)
weighted_top <- inspections |>
  arrange(desc(KNOWN_SEVERITY_SCORE), desc(inspect_dt), encounter) |>
  slice_head(n = 20)
alternative_top <- inspections |>
  arrange(desc(3 * NUM_HIGH + 2 * NUM_MEDIUM + NUM_LOW), desc(inspect_dt), encounter) |>
  slice_head(n = 20)

```

# Introduction

This analysis covers **Allegheny County**, not all of Western Pennsylvania. The combined local exports and scraped Accela PDF reports span `r min(all_inspections$inspect_dt)` through `r max(all_inspections$inspect_dt)`. The 2026 results cover **`r period_start` through `r period_end`**, with `r fmt(nrow(inspections))` inspection encounters and `r fmt(sum(inspections$NUM_VIOLATION_CATEGORIES))` recorded violation-category rows extracted from PDF reports on the Accela Citizens Access portal. This is a partial-year analysis based on available PDF reports, not a complete 2026 ranking.

As a local data scientist, I wanted to make these public records easier to compare while preserving the severity information recorded by inspectors. This ranking is my analytical summary, not an official Health Department grade or an estimate of the probability of foodborne illness.

## What the Health Department's categories mean

The [Allegheny County Health Department (ACHD)](https://www.alleghenycounty.us/Services/Health-Department/Food-Safety/Search-Inspection-Reports) describes three severity levels:

| Severity | Meaning | Examples on ACHD's page |
|:---|:---|:---|
| High | Can directly lead to foodborne illness | Unsafe holding/cooking temperatures; improper employee handwashing |
| Medium | Can increase the chance of foodborne illness | No soap at handwashing sinks; no food probe thermometer; no Certified Food Protection Manager present |
| Low | Usually does not cause foodborne illness on its own; concerns cleanliness, safety, or maintenance | Damaged floors, poorly maintained ventilation hoods, poor lighting |

These are examples, not a fixed severity lookup for all findings in a category. The revised analysis uses the **`high`, `medium`, and `low` flags for each inspection/category** extracted from the inspection report table (including "Imminent" hazard marks under `high`), rather than guessing from `description_new`.

## Counting and ranking rules

1. **Only `rating = V` is a violation.** Other assessment rows are excluded even if severity flags remain populated.
2. **Count categories, not individual findings.** Each row is an inspection/category pair; one category can describe several problems. When multiple severity flags are true, assign that category its highest recorded severity (high, then medium, then low). Thus H, M, and L below are mutually exclusive category counts and may differ from the report's counts of all checked severity boxes.
3. **Keep unclassified violations visible.** A `V` row with no true severity flag is unclassified (U), not low risk or a zero-risk finding. H + M + L + U equals the number of violation categories. In this period, `r fmt(sum(inspections$NUM_UNCLASSIFIED))` categories are unclassified across `r fmt(sum(inspections$NUM_UNCLASSIFIED > 0))` encounters. Rankings based on known severities may understate those encounters.
4. **Primary ranking: H, then M, then L, descending.** More high-severity categories rank ahead of any number of lower-severity categories. This is an explicit analytical choice to prioritize severity; ACHD does not prescribe this ordering of facilities. Identical H/M/L profiles share a rank. Dates and encounter IDs only stabilize display order; a top-20 display can cut a tie.
5. **Secondary score: 5H + 3M + L.** These are analyst-selected weights, not ACHD weights or measured risk ratios. The **known-severity score** omits unclassified categories and is incomplete wherever U > 0. It measures recorded category burden, not safety. No median or quartile is labeled a “clean” or “acceptable” threshold.

## Comparison population and data quality

- Link the inspection and violation exports by **`encounter`**, and group facilities by **`id`**. Names and street addresses are display labels, not identifiers. Separate encounters on the same date remain separate inspections.
- Include encounters from the inspection export even when there are no matching `V` rows. There are `r fmt(sum(inspections$NUM_VIOLATION_CATEGORIES == 0))` such encounters in this period. “Zero recorded violations” is a database result, not proof that every condition was assessed or satisfactory.
- Compare facilities primarily using the mean H/M/L profile of routine visits whose purpose is **“Comprehensive”** (or **“Initial”**). Reinspections, complaints, pre-operational visits, and change-of-ownership encounters can have different scopes. All-encounter averages remain descriptive context. Even routine visits are not a random or fully standardized sample, and facilities with one visit have limited evidence.
- Exclude explicit training-client names by facility ID and export the exclusion list for review. Duplicate encounter/category rows, invalid severity flags, and unmatched inspection metadata stop processing instead of silently changing rankings.

ACHD changed software on **August 11, 2025**; 2026 reports are published as PDF attachments through [Citizens Access](https://aca-prod.accela.com/ALLEGHENYCO/Cap/CapHome.aspx?module=EnvHealth&TabName=Home) and extracted via `scraper/scrape_pdfs.py`. Report links and inspection placards describe those visits, not a facility's current status.

# Stats for Nerds

Distribution of known-severity scores for all recorded inspection encounters in the available 2026 period, including zero-recorded-violation visits:

```{r}
chart <- ggplot(inspections, aes(x = KNOWN_SEVERITY_SCORE)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, boundary = -0.5,
                 fill = "#218C8D",
                 color = "white",
                 alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "The distribution of recorded burden",
    subtitle = "All inspection purposes | Allegheny County, 2026",
    x = "Known-severity score (5H + 3M + L)",
    y = "Inspection encounters"
  ) +
  theme_portfolio()
interactive_chart(chart)
```


```{r}
pct_tbl <- inspections |>
  summarise(
    Min = min(KNOWN_SEVERITY_SCORE),
    Q1 = quantile(KNOWN_SEVERITY_SCORE, 0.25),
    Median = median(KNOWN_SEVERITY_SCORE),
    Mean = mean(KNOWN_SEVERITY_SCORE),
    Q3 = quantile(KNOWN_SEVERITY_SCORE, 0.75),
    Max = max(KNOWN_SEVERITY_SCORE)
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Statistic", values_to = "Score")

kable(pct_tbl, digits = 2, caption = "Known-severity score summary (all purposes)")
```

For facility comparisons, use only Initial/Comprehensive inspections and retain zero-recorded-violation visits in the denominator. This distribution gives each facility one observation: its mean known-severity score over its Initial/Comprehensive inspections in the available period.

```{r}
chart <- ggplot(initial_yearly, aes(x = AVG_INITIAL_SCORE)) +

                 color = "white",
                 alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "A more comparable facility-level view",
    subtitle = "Mean scores on Initial/Comprehensive inspections only | 2026",
    x = "Mean known-severity score (5H + 3M + L)",
    y = "Facilities"
  ) +
  theme_portfolio()
interactive_chart(chart)
```


```{r}
pct_tbl <- initial_yearly |>
  summarise(
    Min = min(AVG_INITIAL_SCORE),
    Q1 = quantile(AVG_INITIAL_SCORE, 0.25),
    Median = median(AVG_INITIAL_SCORE),
    Mean = mean(AVG_INITIAL_SCORE),
    Q3 = quantile(AVG_INITIAL_SCORE, 0.75),
    Max = max(AVG_INITIAL_SCORE)
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Statistic", values_to = "Score")

kable(pct_tbl, digits = 2, caption = "Facility mean score summary (Initial/Comprehensive inspections only)")
```

## Sensitivity to the ranking method

The severity-first and 5/3/1 weighted top-20 inspection lists share **`r length(intersect(severity_top, weighted_top$encounter))` of 20** encounters. Changing the weights to 3/2/1 retains **`r length(intersect(weighted_top$encounter, alternative_top$encounter))` of 20** encounters from the 5/3/1 list. These are descriptive sensitivity checks with deterministic tie-breaking, not statistical confidence measures. The main severity-first ranking does not depend on numerical weights.

# A Visual Tour of the Findings

The HTML report adds hover details, zoom controls, and clickable follow-up bubbles. Render it with `quarto render 2026_hall_of_shame.qmd --to html` and open `2026_Health_Inspections_Interactive.html` in a browser. GitHub's README preview and the PDF use static images. The HTML file is self-contained and can be shared or hosted as a portfolio page.

## Inspection activity and scope

Inspection volume and purpose provide context for the rankings. The chart counts every recorded encounter, including visits with no recorded violations. “Follow-up” includes the exact purposes Reinspection and Partial ReInspection; mixed-purpose and pre-operational/ownership-change visits are grouped with other visits. These monthly counts describe activity in the scraped PDF dataset, not a trend in restaurant safety.

```{r inspection-calendar}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-alt: Monthly stacked columns showing Initial/Comprehensive, follow-up, and other inspection encounters in 2026.
interactive_chart(plot_inspection_activity(inspections, period_label = "2026"), "calendar")
```

## Why category names alone cannot determine severity

Each row below shows the severity mix within one of the 15 most frequently cited categories. A darker cell means a larger share of that category's violation records, not a more dangerous category. The variation is why this analysis uses the inspector's recorded flags instead of assigning every occurrence of a category the same severity.

```{r category-severity}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-alt: Heatmap of the 15 most frequently cited categories, showing percentages classified as high, medium, low, or unclassified.
interactive_chart(plot_category_severity(category_audit, period_label = "2026"), "categories", height = 850)
```

## The composition behind the ranking

The bars below show the mean number of categories at each severity for the top 15 facilities in the Initial/Comprehensive ranking. Facilities are ordered by their severity profile, not by total bar length. The annotations retain the inspection denominator and the number of unclassified categories so the limits of each comparison remain visible.

```{r facility-severity-profiles}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-alt: Horizontal stacked bars showing mean high-, medium-, and low-severity category counts for the 15 highest-ranked facilities on Initial/Comprehensive inspections.
interactive_chart(plot_facility_profiles(initial_yearly, period_label = "2026"), "facilities", height = 950)
```

## What happens at the next recorded follow-up?

Match an Initial/Comprehensive visit to the very next recorded encounter for the same facility only when that encounter is a Reinspection or Partial ReInspection on a later date. Keep the earliest eligible pair per facility within the available 2026 period, then exclude pairs with unclassified categories at either visit. This is chronological matching, not a verified administrative link between reports. Same-day pairs are excluded because the analysis does not use visit times.

Below the diagonal, the follow-up score is lower than the Initial score. Bubble area represents the number of facilities at the same coordinates. These facilities are a selected group that received follow-up visits; changes can reflect both corrections and narrower follow-up scope.

In the HTML version, **hover over a bubble to preview restaurant names; click it to see every facility at that coordinate**, including both visit dates, scores, and report links. The dropdown below the chart also lets you select a facility using a keyboard or touch screen. Accela search links are labeled as searches and include the encounter identifier.

```{r followup-comparison}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-alt: Bubble scatterplot comparing Initial and next recorded follow-up scores, with a diagonal reference line for unchanged scores.
display_followups(followup_pairs, period_label = "2026")
```

# 2026 Rankings: Available Accela Period

Click a facility name for the linked portal. **H/M/L** are category counts at the highest recorded severity; **U** is the number of unclassified categories. The tables describe recorded conditions during this period, not current operating conditions.

## Inspections ranked by recorded severity

```{r}
inspections |>
  slice_head(n = 20) |>
  select(name, Rank = SEVERITY_RANK, Date = inspect_dt, Purpose = purpose,
         H = NUM_HIGH, M = NUM_MEDIUM, L = NUM_LOW, U = NUM_UNCLASSIFIED, REPORT) |>
  report_table("Top 20 inspection encounters by H, then M, then L")
```

## Secondary view: weighted category burden

This list allows several lower-severity categories to outweigh a higher-severity category. It answers a different question from the main ranking. The score is incomplete when U > 0.

```{r}
weighted_top |>
  select(name, Date = inspect_dt, Purpose = purpose, Score = KNOWN_SEVERITY_SCORE,
         H = NUM_HIGH, M = NUM_MEDIUM, L = NUM_LOW, U = NUM_UNCLASSIFIED, REPORT) |>
  report_table("Top 20 encounters by known-severity score (5H + 3M + L)")
```

## Facilities ranked using Initial/Comprehensive inspections

Order facilities by mean H, then mean M, then mean L across Initial/Comprehensive inspections only. **N** is the number of those inspections; **U** is their total unclassified category count. A high mean based on N = 1 does not establish a pattern of repeated problems. Links go to each facility's latest recorded encounter in the period, which may be a reinspection rather than an Initial visit.

```{r}
initial_yearly |>
  slice_head(n = 20) |>
  select(name, Rank = SEVERITY_RANK, N = NUM_INITIAL_INSPECTIONS,
         `Mean H` = AVG_INITIAL_HIGH, `Mean M` = AVG_INITIAL_MEDIUM,
         `Mean L` = AVG_INITIAL_LOW, U = NUM_INITIAL_UNCLASSIFIED, REPORT) |>
  report_table("Top 20 facilities by mean Initial/Comprehensive-inspection severity profile", digits = 2)
```

## Follow-up context for those facilities

For the same facilities, **N** counts all encounter purposes and **Mean** is the all-encounter mean known-severity score, including zero-recorded-violation visits. **Latest** is the score for the linked encounter; **U** is its unclassified category count. The mean also omits unclassified categories on earlier visits; their totals are retained in the CSV. A lower follow-up score can reflect corrections or a narrower inspection scope, so it does not prove that all previous problems were resolved.

```{r}
initial_yearly |>
  slice_head(n = 20) |>
  select(name, N = NUM_INSPECTIONS, Mean = AVG_KNOWN_SEVERITY_SCORE,
         Date = LATEST_INSPECTION_DATE, Purpose = LATEST_PURPOSE,
         Latest = LATEST_KNOWN_SEVERITY_SCORE, U = LATEST_NUM_UNCLASSIFIED, REPORT) |>
  report_table("All-encounter and latest-visit context for the facilities above", digits = 2)
```


# Discussion

The category summaries cannot convey all the detail in an inspector's narrative. Here are selected excerpts from the 2026 Accela inspection reports, along with each encounter's severity-first rank, weighted-score rank, and placard status:

**[Da Village Social Club and Event Center, Greenway Dr, 03/17/2026](data/accela_downloads/FSP-PERM-202603170185/_FoodSafety_Inspection_Report_567_20260317_163113.pdf)** *(Severity Rank #13, Weighted Score Rank #4 — Follow Up Required)*:

- Facility has been serving food prepared in a private home. *REPEAT VIOLATION*

- Evidence of vomit and fecal matter present in men's toilet room upstairs, including toilet and both handwashing sinks, not properly cleaned up.

- Hand sink in men's restroom upstairs clogged with vomit residue.

- Hookah/nicotine items found stored in box with food items.

- Non essential items stored throughout in numerous rooms, including mattress and bed frame in the kitchen area.

- Carbon monoxide hazard - water heater flume pitch is negative (pointing downwards).

**[Kirkland's Bussin Kitchen, Broadway Ave, 09/10/2026](data/accela_downloads/FSP-PERM-202603030140/FoodSafety_Inspection_Report_567_DIT_20260910_231639.pdf)** *(Severity Rank #306, Weighted Score Rank #306 — Ordered To Close)*:

- Facility found open and operating under a closure order issued by the Allegheny County Health Department.

- Front door found propped open concealing the closure placard placed on the outer glass of the door.

- Complaint in Equity served to Eric Kirkland of Kirklands Bussin LLC... Stowe Twp police present during the service.

**[Paradise Island Hookah Lounge, Duquesne Plz, 03/05/2026](data/accela_downloads/FSP-PERM-202603050141/_FoodSafety_Inspection_Report_567_20260306_120945.pdf)** *(Severity Rank #47, Weighted Score Rank #19 — Ordered To Close)*:

- A pan of spoiled raw chicken. Chicken has a strong odor, slimy, and is discolored.

- Dog feces found on the floor under a swing in the swing bar room. Animals are not allowed in food facilities.

**[Pulse Overlly Loaded, N Dallas Ave, 08/05/2026](data/accela_downloads/FSP-PERM-202608110472/_FoodSafety_Inspection_Report_567_DIT_20260811_115238.pdf)** *(Severity Rank #12, Weighted Score Rank #1 — Ordered To Close)*:

- No hot water supplied to various critical sinks throughout the facility. *IMMINENT HAZARD*

- Wastewater from handwashing sink in restroom near main bar observed collecting into large plastic bowl; not properly plumbed into wastewater line.

- Several house flies observed throughout the facility (>5 flies; too many to count).

- Evidence of roof leak observed in kitchen area (water damage causing ceiling collapse in minor spots).

- Inspection conducted in conjunction with the Nuisance Bar Task Force.

\pagebreak

**[Cafe Vivella, Babcock Blvd, 08/11/2026](data/accela_downloads/FSP-PERM-202606160368/_FoodSafety_Inspection_Report_567_20260730_111259.pdf)** *(Severity Rank #8, Weighted Score Rank #13 — Reinspection Scheduled)*:

- Sandals in handwashing sink. Removed during inspection.

- Observed a child in food prep area at start of inspection.

- Observed PIC place soiled dishes from the dining room onto food prep counter and cutting board.

- Operator not knowledgeable on food safety with regards to personal hygiene, cold holding, sanitizing, cross contamination and food storage.

**[Urban Air Adventure Park, E Waterfront Dr, 07/06/2026](data/accela_downloads/FSP-PERM-202603200190/_FoodSafety_Inspection_Report_567_DIT_20260706_124753.pdf)** *(Severity Rank #42, Weighted Score Rank #113 — Inspected & Permitted)*:

- Numerous pieces of candy in the Candy Locker vending machine have been chewed open and through. Food and package debris can be seen throughout the machine. Operator has turned the machine off prior to inspection. Machine was still found in front customer area.

- Rodent droppings can be seen throughout the facility, including... Around the Dip n Dots chest freezer [and] Inside of the vending machine.

- Decomposing rodent found on a trap in the Loading Dock room.

**[Red Robin Gourmet Burgers and Brews, E Waterfront Dr, 08/31/2026](data/accela_downloads/FSP-PERM-202608260503/FoodSafety_Inspection_Report_567_20260831_121704.pdf)** *(Severity Rank #98, Weighted Score Rank #113 — Inspected & Permitted)*:

- Two dead mice were seen in glue boards under booths.

- Three dead mice were seen in glue boards in cabinet with electrical panel box in server area.

- Two mice, one live and one dead, were seen in glue boards under cold well for dressings in server area.

**[Chaai & Chaatwala, Centre Ave, 08/18/2026](data/accela_downloads/FSP-PERM-202608180487/_FoodSafety_Inspection_Report_567_20260818_150031.pdf)** *(Severity Rank #14, Weighted Score Rank #7 — Ordered To Close)*:

- When asked the PIC stated warewashing procedures were to sanitize, wash, and then rinse dishes.

**[Grand Mart, Arlington Ave, 07/29/2026](data/accela_downloads/FSP-PERM-202607290453/_FoodSafety_Inspection_Report_567_20260729_135315.pdf)** *(Severity Rank #156, Weighted Score Rank #68 — Inspected & Permitted)*:

---

Health inspections are a snapshot of how a food facility is operating at a specific point in time, not a permanent verdict. Severity, inspection scope, and follow-up findings matter more than a single league-table position. Read the full report and check recent inspections before drawing conclusions about a facility today.

Questions and suggestions on my methodology are welcome. Thanks for reading!

[Source code](https://github.com/Elkip/West-PA-Health-Inspection-Analysis/tree/master)

# Reproducing the Analysis

Interactive HTML additionally requires `plotly`, `htmlwidgets`, and `htmltools`: install them with `install.packages(c("plotly", "htmlwidgets", "htmltools"))`. With Quarto installed, run `quarto render 2026_hall_of_shame.qmd --to html`. The generated HTML embeds its JavaScript and works offline; opening the linked inspection reports requires internet access.

Use R 4.1 or later with `dplyr` (1.1.0 or later), `tidyr`, `ggplot2`, `stringr`, `scales`, and `knitr`. Packages must be built for a compatible version of R. From the repository root:

1. Save the [historical violation export](https://data.wprdc.org/datastore/dump/1a1329e2-418c-4bd3-af2c-cc334e7559af) as `data/wprdc_violations.csv` and the matching [historical inspection export](https://data.wprdc.org/datastore/dump/4ea730d8-2bf9-4783-b0a5-b41ed687097e) as `data/wprdc_inspections.csv`, then run `python3 scraper/scrape_pdfs.py --combine` to extract the Accela PDF reports (`data/accela_inspections.csv` and `data/accela_violations.csv`) and merge both sources into `data/inspections.csv` and `data/violations.csv`.
2. Run `Rscript clean_inspections.r` to generate the summaries in `out/`.
3. Run `Rscript tests/test_inspection_analysis.R` to check scoring and aggregation, including two comparisons with original inspection PDFs when the local exports are available. Run `Rscript tests/test_followup_matching.R` to check the follow-up chart's matching rules.
4. Run `Rscript render_readme.r` to regenerate `README.md` (and `2026_README.md`) and plots from the Quarto documents. For a PDF, install Quarto and a TeX distribution and run `quarto render 2026_hall_of_shame.qmd --to pdf`.

Generated files:

- `out/violations_by_inspection.csv`: all encounters in the shared export window, purpose, severity counts, unclassified counts, known-severity score, and `SCORE_COMPLETE` (whether every recorded violation category has a severity).
- `out/violations_by_year.csv`: facility/year summaries, Initial/Comprehensive-only and all-encounter means, denominators, and latest-report context within each year.
- `out/category_severity_audit.csv`: recorded severity distribution by category and year across the shared window; the visualizations use only 2026.
- `out/coverage.csv`: date bounds and record counts after training-client exclusions.
- `out/excluded_training_facilities.csv`: excluded facility identifiers and names.
